front: Describing a graph: what four things to include?
back: Overall trend, figures with units, anomalies and (where relevant) a comparison.
A map in which areas are shaded by class of value; it hides variation within each area.

front: Proportional symbols: how do radii scale?
back: Area is proportional to the value, so radius is proportional to the square root of the value.

front: Names of isolines: rainfall, pressure, temperature, height?

back: A flow map (arrows whose width shows amount) or a desire-line map.
To show a very wide range of values on one graph; each step is a tenfold increase.
Source and purpose, date, scale and classes, axis start, sample and whether the data are estimated.
Describe says what the pattern is (with figures); explain gives reasons. Do not explain when asked to describe.
